name: Digit 360

sources.title: M. Lambeta et al., "Digitizing Touch with an Artificial Multimodal Fingertip", arXiv:2411.02479v1, 4 Nov 2024
sources.covers: sensing principle, "approximately 8.3 million taxels", camera frame rate (240 fps) and pixel size (1.1 um), solid immersion hyper-fisheye lens, USB 3.0 to the host, comparison table (Table 5: sample rate 10,000 Hz, area 2340 mm^2, spatial resolution 0.007 mm, force resolutions)

note: A contact sensor, modelled by pad coverage, not a workspace camera, so it has no imagers. A finger-shaped, omnidirectional visuotactile fingertip (research platform from Meta FAIR; the paper also describes pressure, temperature, audio/vibration sensing and an on-device AI accelerator). Figures from the paper: a CMOS camera at 240 fps with 1.1 um pixels behind a custom solid immersion hyper-fisheye lens; "approximately 8.3 million taxels" (the image pixels; no width and height are stated, so camera_resolution is null and no stream is entered); the comparison table gives a sensing area of 2340 mm^2 (entered as area_mm2: the curved surface has no stated width and height, so pad_mm is null), a 10,000 Hz sample rate (the non-visual channels; vibrations "upwards to 10 kHz"), spatial resolution 0.007 mm, normal and shear force resolutions 1.01 mN and 1.27 mN. Host link USB 3.0. Not stated: power, mass, size (the fingertip is described as of human-fingertip size, no dimensions), stream format.
